root_cause: The currently actionable failure is a synthesis/frontend hang in rtl/rename_unit.sv, not a simulation behavior bug: the checkpoint-save allocation loop writes a row of the 2D unpacked checkpoint array with a variable row index (`ckpt_map_nxt[alloc_slot][i] = spec_map_nxt[i]`), which makes yosys read_verilog explode. Bisection shows removing just those writes drops yosys from >15 s to 1.1 s. The functional TB currently passes, and the FIFO->bitmap free-list refactor is already correct; row-decode every such write into constant-index rows and audit all other unpacked-array writes in the same file.
repair_constraints: Never rename ports, modules, or files; keep the rv32i5/rename_unit interface contract unchanged.
Preserve all currently passing TB behavior; the synthesis fix must be behavior-preserving and must not change cycle-level functional behavior.
Do not modify or revert the already-correct FIFO->bitmap free-list refactor.
Rewrite every variable-row-index write into a 2D unpacked array as a constant-index row-decoded write; audit ckpt_map_nxt and any other 2D unpacked arrays in rename_unit.sv.
Bit-vector arrays such as slot_* and free_vec_nxt are not subject to this restriction, but their semantics must remain unchanged.
After the patch, yosys read_verilog must complete without hanging while all existing functional tests remain passing.
evidence: Repair state: 'yosys read_verilog hangs on rtl/rename_unit.sv'; bisection proved the checkpoint-save loop writes `ckpt_map_nxt[alloc_slot][i] = spec_map_nxt[i]` with a variable row index; removing just these 3 lines drops yosys from >15s hang to 1.1s. Also: 'TB PASSES; one synthesizability defect remains' and 'FIFO->bitmap refactor already landed and is correct; do not touch it.' The teacher brief's bench_ooo_overlap64 is not the active blocker in this current RTL state.
